note: Every record below is real, drawn from named, publicly accessible sources — Stanford HAI's AI Index, McKinsey's State of AI global survey, the IEA's Energy and AI research, and an open-access arXiv paper. isDemo is false on every record. Figures are cited as facts with attribution, never as reproduced source text, per docs/DATA_POLICY.md. Self-reported and modeled figures are marked with Medium/Low confidence and explained in each record's notes.

records.licenseBasis: Publicly accessible news report of a company's own public announcement; figure cited as fact with attribution, no reproduction of article text (fair use)
records.notes: Self-reported by OpenAI, not independently audited. Up from 800 million in October 2025. OpenAI does not officially publish monthly active user figures.

records.metricName: Organizations reporting regular AI use in at least one business function
records.sourceTitle: The State of AI: Global Survey 2025
records.licenseBasis: Publicly accessible report; survey statistic cited as fact with attribution, no reproduction of report text (fair use)
records.notes: Self-reported survey data from 1,993 respondents across 105 countries — not an audited census. Up from 78% in McKinsey's prior-year (2024) survey.

Equivalent to about 1.5% of world electricity consumption in 2024. A later IEA update (2026) puts 2025 consumption at roughly 485 TWh, growing ~17% year over year — see IEA 'Key Questions on Energy and AI'.

records.calculationMethod: IEA's own aggregate estimate of global data-centre capital investment, reported as having 'nearly doubled since 2022' to reach approximately half a trillion dollars in 2024.
records.notes: IEA states this as an approximate, rounded figure ('half a trillion dollars'), not a precise audited total.

records.licenseBasis: Publicly accessible report; statistic cited as fact with attribution, no reproduction of report text (fair use)
records.calculationMethod: Aggregated from Quid's private-market deal-tracking dataset plus disclosed corporate AI capital expenditure, as compiled by the Stanford AI Index. Includes both private investment (a subset, $344.7B) and broader corporate capex.
records.notes: Up from an estimated $253 billion in 2024 per the same source series. Reflects Quid's methodology and disclosed-spend aggregation, not a single audited total.

records.metricName: AI research output at five leading AI/ML conferences
records.sourceTitle: The Shift Toward Open and Reproducible AI Research
records.licenseBasis: arXiv preprint, open access; statistic cited as fact with attribution, no reproduction of paper text (fair use)
records.calculationMethod: Manual analysis of 56,800 papers from five top AI/ML conferences (AAAI, ICLR, ICML, IJCAI, NeurIPS) published 2014–2024, as documented in the cited paper.
records.notes: Up from 1,206 papers in 2014 at the same five conferences — roughly a tenfold increase over the decade. Covers major conference venues only, not journals or general preprints.
